g.text: bf16 trades precision for fp32's range

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #0f172a
font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: bf16 and fp32 share an 8-bit exponent, so a bf16 cast never overflows where fp32 would not — which is exactly why bf16 replaced

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: fp16 for training and why loss scaling became unnecessary. fp16's 5-bit exponent tops out at 65504, and gradients underflow long

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #475569

g.text: before that. The price of bf16 is 7 mantissa bits, which is why norms and reductions are still computed in fp32.
